newsitem.title: UK: EMU clause assures Eurobond liquidity - bankers.
newsitem.headline: EMU clause assures Eurobond liquidity - bankers.

text.p: Eurobonds with special EMU-oriented clauses will prove more liquid than those without such language, primary market players said on Thursday.
Eurobonds which cannot be redenominated in the euro at the same time as government bonds switch over -- widely expected to be January 1, 1999 -- may quickly become illiquid, they said.

"The (euro) clause is more than just a marketing twist," said a syndicate manager at a Morgan Stanley in Paris, lead manager of a recent euro deal. "It is an innovation investors appreciate because liquidity will be better for euro bonds."

"For other bonds after EMU it (liquidity) depends on the size and name. If you have, say, a five billion franc deal from a good name you would expect that to remain liquid. Otherwise, I'm not so sure," he added.
The past month has seen the launch of the first Eurobonds with clauses allowing for their redenomination in euros after the third stage of European economic and monetary union.

These euro Eurobonds are being sold in European currencies, including the Ecu, and will be traded in that currency until EMU. Most will be fungible with other issues the borrower might launch in the future, creating jumbo euro Eurobonds.
J.P. Morgan, which led the first euro deal, Austria in francs, has said euro bonds will be super liquid because of their size and because of the pan-European aspect after EMU.
But other parts of the Eurobond market would be fragmented and illiquid, it said.
